_source.note: flavorText and tagline come from the Roles chapter; roleAbility.summary from that chapter's overview; roleAbility.mechanicalText transcribed in full from the detailed Role Abilities chapter (Cyberpunk RED Core Rulebook, pp. 144-163), including the per-rank tables. In-world quote sidebars and 'in Action' examples were omitted; in-book page references were removed for in-app use.

_rules.note: Every Character sets their Role's Role Ability to Rank 4 at creation, in all three methods.

rockerboy.name: Rockerboy
rockerboy.tagline: Rock-and-roll rebels who use performance, art, and rhetoric to fight authority.
rockerboy.flavorText: If you live to rock, this is where you belong. As a Rockerboy, you're one of the street poets, the social conscience, and the rebels of the Time of the Red. With the advent of digital porta-studios and garage music mastering, every Rockerboy with a message can take it to The Street, put it in the record stores, bounce it off the comsats. Sometimes, your message isn't something the Corporations or the government wants to hear. Sometimes what you say is going to get right in the faces of the powerful people who really want to run this world. But you don't care, because as a Rockerboy, you know it's your place to challenge authority, whether in straight-out protest songs that tell it like it is, playing kick-ass rock n' roll to get the people away from the TV sets and into The Streets, firing up the crowd with speeches, or composing fiery writings that shape the minds and hearts of millions. You have a proud history as a Rockerboy. Dylan, Springsteen, U2, NWA, the Who, Jett, the Stones—the legions of hard-rock heroes who told the truth with screaming guitars or gut-honest lyrics. You have the power to get the people up; to lead, inspire, and inform. Your message can give the timid courage, the weak strength, and the blind vision. Rockerboy legends like Johnny Silverhand, Rockerboy Manson (for whom the Role is named) and Kerry Eurodyne have led armies against Corporations and governments. Rockerboys have exposed corruption and brought down dictators. It's a lot of power for someone doing gigs every night in another city. But you can handle it. After all: you came to play!

roleAbility.name: Charismatic Impact
roleAbility.summary: The Rockerboy's Role Ability is Charismatic Impact. With this ability, they can influence others by sheer presence of personality. They need not be a musical performer; they can influence others through poetry, art, dance, or simply their physical presence. They could be a rocker—or a cult leader. As they grow in skill, they can affect larger and larger groups and call on their fans for greater and greater requests of loyalty.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Rockerboy's Role Ability is Charismatic Impact. They can influence others by sheer presence of personality — through music, poetry, art, dance, or simply their physical presence. They could be a rocker, or a cult leader.

A Rockerboy can only use Charismatic Impact on Fans. Outside of combat you can turn non-fans into fans (unless they actively dislike you) by rolling Charismatic Impact + 1d10 vs. DV8 for a single person, DV10 for a Small Group of up to 6, or DV12 for a Huge Group. The GM decides when someone you meet is already a Fan.

When you ask a favor of a fan or group, the GM checks the favor against your current Rank. If it's beyond your Rank you automatically fail. Otherwise group size sets the DV and you roll Charismatic Impact + 1d10. On a success the fans give their best effort; on a failure you can't ask that same favor of those fans again for a week. Each Rank sets the best venue you can play and what you can ask of a single fan (DV8), a small group of up to 6 (DV10), and a huge group (DV12):

Ranks 1–2 — Venues: small local clubs. Single: a small favor (buy you a drink/meal, give you a lift). Small Group: fans ask for autographs and stop you in the street. Huge Group: none yet.
Ranks 3–4 — Venues: well-known clubs. Single: a major favor (put in a good word, etc.). Small Group: regularly hang out and supply party favors. Huge Group: a strong local following that buys your recordings and merch.
Ranks 5–6 — Venues: large, important clubs. Single: commit a minor crime (shoplift, help in a fight). Small Group: act as your personal posse. Huge Group: loyal fans across the City doing major favors for attention.
Ranks 7–8 — Venues: small concert halls, local video feed. Single: risk their life for you without question. Small Group: commit a minor crime for you. Huge Group: rabidly loyal — they fight rival fans and band together to help you.
Rank 9 — Venues: large concert halls, national video feed. Single: commit a major crime. Small Group: commit a major crime. Huge Group: a cult-like following that will riot, destroy property, even kill for you.
Rank 10 — Venues: huge stadiums or international video. Single: sacrifice themselves for you without question. Small Group: risk their lives as personal protection. Huge Group: a worldwide, cult-like following — effectively a private army built on your charisma.

solo.name: Solo
solo.tagline: Assassins, bodyguards, killers, and soldiers-for-hire in a lawless new world.
solo.flavorText: You were reborn with a gun in your hand—the flesh and blood hand—not the metallic weapons factory that covers most of your other arm. Whether as a freelance guard and killer-for-hire, or as one of the Corporate cybersoldiers who enforce business deals and the Company's "black operations," you're one of the elite fighting machines of the Time of the Red. Most Solos put in military time during the 4th Corporate War, in a Corporate army, or in one of the government's current "police actions" around the country. As the battle damage piles up, you start to rely more and more upon tech: cyberlimbs for weapons and armor, bio-program chips to increase your reflexes and awareness, combat drugs to give you that edge over your opponents. When you're the best of the best, you might even leave the ranks of Corporate samurai and go ronin—freelancing your lethal talents as a killer, bodyguard, or enforcer to whoever can pay your very high fees. Sounds good? There's a price—a heavy one. You've lost so much of your original meat body that you're almost a machine. Your killing reflexes are so jacked up that you have to restrain yourself from going berserk at any moment. Years of combat drugs taken to keep the edge have given you terrifying addictions. There are few people you can trust anymore. One night you might sleep in a penthouse condo in the City, the next in a filthy alley on The Street. But that's the price of being the best. And you're willing to pay it. Because you're a Solo.

roleAbility.name: Combat Awareness
roleAbility.summary: The Solo's Role Ability is Combat Awareness. With Combat Awareness, a Solo can call up their training to have an enhanced situational awareness of the battlefield. When combat begins, anytime outside of combat, or in combat with an Action, a Solo may divide the total number of points they have in their Combat Awareness Role Ability among a number of combat abilities. If a Solo chooses to not change their point assignments, their previous ones persist. Activating some of these abilities will cost the Solo more points than others.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
When combat begins (before Initiative is rolled), anytime outside of combat, or in combat with an Action, a Solo may divide the total points they have in their Combat Awareness Role Ability among the abilities below. If they don't change their assignments, the previous ones persist. Some abilities cost more points than others.

Damage Deflection — trained to roll with the punches. For 2 points decrease the first damage you take this Round by 1; 4 points by 2; 6 points by 3; 8 points by 4; 10 points by 5.
Fumble Recovery — for 4 points, you ignore critical failures (natural 1s) rolled while attacking. Those rolls still count as a 1.
Initiative Reaction — each point adds +1 to your Initiative rolls.
Precision Attack — for 3 points, +1 to any Attacks; 6 points, +2; 9 points, +3.
Spot Weakness — each point adds +1 to the damage (before armor) of your first successful Attack in a Round.
Threat Detection — each point adds +1 to any Perception Checks.

netrunner.name: Netrunner
netrunner.tagline: Cybernetic master hackers of the post-NET world and brain-burning secret stealers.
netrunner.flavorText: You're a brain-burning computer hacker & master of the Post-NET cyberverse in the Time of the Red. At three, your parents bought you an old Kirama LPD-12 cyberdeck with Zetatech 526 optical goggles (you were too young for interface plugs), and your life was changed. By fifth grade, you were already using REFRAME-G1s meta-programming to crack into the school district's system and change your grades. When you were thirteen, you shifted enough funds out of unprotected Trans United Bank accounts to finance your first neural interface plugs. You couldn't wait to run high and fast with the other gods of the NET—Bartmoss, Magnificent Curtis, and the rest. Then the 4th Corp War blew the Old NET apart. The R.A.B.I.D.S. made NET travel a suicide run; the Nodes were fragmented or corrupted. But there were still places to run. You just had to go there and jack in the hard way. You traded in sitting on the couch for a Bodyweight combat bodysuit and Virtuality 5 interface goggles to mesh NET with Meatspace. The systems you cracked were smaller, but even deadlier. Now, you're really part of a team, with Solos to cover your back, Medtechs to restart your heart if the ICE gets you, and Techs to help you hot-wire your cyberdeck for more speed and software deployment. Now, nothing can stop you. As an electronic wraith, you slip into the "hardest" mainframe systems with ease: stealing, trading, and selling their deepest secrets at will. The Black ICE may still kill you in the end, but until the ride runs out you'll be there, bare-brained and headfirst in the New NET.

roleAbility.name: Interface
roleAbility.summary: The Netrunner's Role Ability is Interface. Interface is what allows the Netrunner to Netrun—to interface with electronic mind-modems (called cyberdecks) to control computers, electronics, and associated programming. The Interface Role Ability also gives the Netrunner access to a wide suite of Abilities related to computer hacking and system control.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
A Netrunner's Interface Role Ability lets them Netrun, sets how many NET Actions they take on their Turn, and grants a suite of Interface Abilities. (The full Netrunning rules are covered separately.)

NET Actions per Turn by Interface Rank: Rank 1–3 = 2 actions; Rank 4–6 = 3; Rank 7–9 = 4; Rank 10 = 5.

Interface Abilities:
Backdoor — break through Passwords and other obstructions in the Architecture.
Cloak — hide your actions in the Architecture before you leave.
Control — control things attached to the Architecture.
Eye-Dee — identify a found piece of data and its value.
Pathfinder — learn the “map” of the Architecture.
Scanner — find the locations of systems in an area.
Slide — slip away from one Black ICE that is following you.
Virus — leave a custom virus at the core of the Architecture.
Zap — a basic Netrunner attack that works against both Programs and other Netrunners.

tech.name: Tech
tech.tagline: Renegade mechanics and supertech inventors; the people who make the Dark Future run.
tech.flavorText: You can't leave anything alone—if it sits near you for more than five minutes, you've disassembled it and made it into something new. You've always got at least two screwdrivers and a wrench in your pockets. Computer down? No problem. Hydrogen burner out in your Metrocar? No problem. Can't get the video to run or your interface glitching? No problem. You make your living building, fixing, and modifying—a crucial occupation in a technological world recovering from a War that broke the back of the supply chain. You can make some good bucks fixing everyday stuff, but for the serious money you need to tackle the big jobs. Illegal weapons. Illegal or stolen cybertech. Corporate espionage and counter-espionage gear for "black operations." If you're any good, you're making a lot of money. And that money goes into new gadgets, hardware, and information. Your black market work isn't just making you friends—it's also racking you up an impressive number of enemies as well—so you invest a lot in defense systems and, if really pushed to the wall, call in a few markers on a Solo or two. You've fixed up tech for everybody from black ops Corporate samurai to Ms. Zepada down the block. No one's ever come back to you with a complaint but that might be because of the turrets guarding your front door. You're addicted to technology in all its forms and that's what makes you a Tech.

roleAbility.name: Maker
roleAbility.summary: A Tech can fix, improve, modify, make, and invent items using Maker, their Role Ability. Each time their Maker Rank rises they gain a Rank in two Maker Specialties of their choice: Field Expertise, Upgrade Expertise, Fabrication Expertise, or Invention Expertise.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
A Tech can fix, improve, modify, make, and invent new items using Maker, their Role Ability. Whenever a Tech increases their Maker Rank by 1, they gain 1 Rank in two different Maker Specialties (Field Expertise, Upgrade Expertise, Fabrication Expertise, or Invention Expertise) of their choice.

Field Expertise — Add your Rank in this Specialty to any Basic Tech, Cybertech, Electronics/Security Tech, Weaponstech, or Land/Sea/Air Vehicle Tech Skill Check made for a non-Maker purpose. With at least 1 Rank, instead of a lengthy full repair you can jury-rig a target to perfect condition (full SP and HP) as an Action at the item's normal repair DV, adding your Field Expertise Rank. The fix holds 10 minutes per Rank, after which the item reverts and can't be jury-rigged again until fully repaired.

Upgrade Expertise — Improve an item in one of the listed ways (an item can benefit from only one such upgrade): e.g. lower non-borgware cyberware Humanity Loss by 1d6 (if normally 2d6+), add a slot, halve future repair time, make a one-handed weapon concealable, raise Average to Excellent quality, add an Attachment Slot or non-basic ammo to an Exotic weapon, +1 SP (if it had any), a Nomad-Rank-1 vehicle upgrade, or install one of your own inventions. Roll TECH + the item's usual repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10; buy materials of the item's price category (consumed). DV and time scale with price category. On a failure you start over, but materials and item are unharmed.

Fabrication Expertise — Build an existing or self-invented item from materials. Roll TECH + the item's usual repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10; buy materials one price category below the item (Super Luxury items need materials worth half their Price). DV and time scale with price category; a failure means starting over with materials intact.

Invention Expertise — Invent a new item or upgrade. Describe its function to the GM in terms of existing technology; if approved, the GM sets its rules and a Price Category (minimum Expensive). Roll TECH + the relevant repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10. Once invented, it can be built with Fabrication or Upgrade Expertise. The GM may rebalance an invention over time.

Upgrade / Fabricate / Invent DV & Time by cost: Cheap/Everyday DV9, 1 hour; Costly DV13, 6 hours; Premium DV17, 1 day; Expensive DV21, 1 week; Very Expensive DV24, 2 weeks; Luxury DV29, 1 month; Super Luxury DV29, 1 month per 10,000eb of Cost.

medtech.name: Medtech
medtech.tagline: Unsanctioned street doctors and cyberware medics, patching up meat and metal alike.
medtech.flavorText: You're an artist, and the human body is your canvas. You've got the best tools the Time of the Red can offer, and you know how to use them. If you're lucky, you got to attend one of the real med schools scattered around the wreck of the Old United States. And after the War, military hospitals were everywhere and the few doctors on the war front needed helping hands to hold down screaming patients and splice cyberware back together. So, maybe you learned that way. And there's always an old ripperdoc or two out there who hearken back to that old science fiction story called The Bladerunner—not that old flatscreen vid, but the really old sci-fi book about renegade doctors who performed illegal street surgery in one of the first dystopian novels. Maybe one of those guys trained you. Maybe that's where you are right now, patching up the wounded, mending up the sick, and keeping the locals alive. For love, commitment, or maybe a just a fat payday on the side. If you're really lucky, you've scored a berth in the local Trauma Team franchise. Trauma Teams are groups of licensed paramedicals who patrol the city looking for patients. You operate from an AV-4 Urban Assault Vehicle, redesigned into an ambulance configuration, and armed with a belly-mounted minigun. It's the best of the best—Trauma Team charges some heavy subscription fees to save its clients, and that translates into new medical toys, faster AV ambulances, and hefty salaries for the best surgeons around. It doesn't matter how you got here. What matters is that you're here, on The Street, doing the job. And you'd be doing it no matter what the reason. It's what marks you as a Medtech.

roleAbility.name: Medicine
roleAbility.summary: The Medtech's Role Ability is Medicine. With this ability, Medtechs can keep people alive who should be dead with their knowledge, tools, and training. In the Time of the Red, they are as much doctors as they are mechanics, caring for people who are often more machine than human. Whenever the Medtech increases their Medicine Rank, they also choose one of three Medicine Specialties to allocate a single point to: surgery, pharmaceuticals, or cryosystems operation.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Medtech Role Ability is Medicine. Whenever the Medtech increases their Medicine Rank, they allocate 1 point to one of three Specialties: Surgery, Medical Tech (Pharmaceuticals), or Medical Tech (Cryosystem Operation). The Medical rules add uses of the Surgery and Medical Tech Skills available only to Medtechs — including cyberware installation and harvesting, bodysculpting, and therapy.

Surgery — Each point gives 2 points in the Surgery Skill (max 10). Surgery is the TECH Skill for treating the most severe Critical Injuries and implanting cyberware, available to Medtechs only through this Specialty.

Medical Tech (Pharmaceuticals) — Each point gives 1 point in the Medical Tech Skill (max 10; max 5 points in this Specialty). Each point also unlocks one pharmaceutical you can synthesize with a DV13 Medical Tech Check (materials wasted on a failure); from 200eb of materials you make doses equal to your Medical Tech Skill in 1 hour. You can't synthesize Street Drugs this way. Drugs: Antibiotic (a naturally healing target heals +2 HP/day for a week; one at a time); Rapidetox (immediately purges a drug, poison, or intoxicant); Speedheal (a non-Mortally-Wounded target heals BODY + WILL HP; once per day); Stim (ignore Seriously Wounded penalties for an hour; once per day); Surge (function without sleep for 24 hours; once per week). Administering a dose takes an Action; an unwilling target can be hit with an Airhypo Melee Attack to dose them instead of dealing damage. Only a Medtech can administer these correctly.

Medical Tech (Cryosystem Operation) — Each point gives 1 point in the Medical Tech Skill (max 10; max 5 points here). Benefits by points: 1 — one Cryopump; 2 — Registered Cryotank Technician with 24/7 access to 1 cryotank at a time at any corporate or government facility; 3 — one Cryotank installed in a room of your choice; 4 — two more Cryotanks (same room) and a Cryopump with 2 charges carrying up to 2 people in stasis; 5 — three more Cryotanks and a Cryopump with 3 charges carrying up to 3 people. Your Medical Tech Skill Level equals your Pharmaceuticals points plus your Cryosystem Operation points.

media.name: Media
media.tagline: Reporters, media stars, and social influencers risking it all for the truth—or glory.
media.flavorText: They're bending the truth out there. And you're going to stop them. Someone has to do it. The Corporations used to rule the world. They dumped toxics, destabilized economies, and committed murder with equal impunity. The government back then couldn't even stop them—hell, they owned the government. But then the War came. The War stripped away the facade and let us all know exactly what had been going on under our noses. And the people who made sure we all knew the score were the Medias. That's you. You've got a vidlink and a press pass, and you're not afraid to use them. You're a city-wide figure, seen nightly all over the Data Pool in the Time of the Red. It's not like the old days, when you had a major Mediacorp behind you; this time, you've gotta depend on your fans, your contacts, and your own reputation. But it's harder for these new Corps to make you disappear. So when you dig down for the dirt and slime the corrupt officials and Corporate lapdogs try to cover up, you can dig deep. The next morning, you can put the details of their crimes all over the screamsheets and vidscreens. Three or four times, the bad guys have tried to kill you—that's why your backup's a crack Solo bodyguard and you've got one of the top ‘Runners in the business digging through NET Architectures to back your stories. You have to be good, or else. Your ‘Runner's just phoned in with a hot lead. You grab your gear and flag your backup. You're going to break those bastards. This time, for sure.

roleAbility.name: Credibility
roleAbility.summary: The Media's Role Ability is Credibility. The Media can not only convince an audience of the truth of what they publish but also has a larger audience the more credible they are. Medias also have greater levels of access to sources and information; they are always in the know with their ears to the ground to pick up on rumors and information passively.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Media Role Ability is Credibility. A Media can convince an audience of what they publish, reaches a larger audience the more credible they are, has greater access to sources and information, and passively picks up rumors.

Rumors — As long as you aren't entirely off-grid, at least twice per week the GM secretly rolls your Credibility Rank + 1d10; if it beats a DV on the Rumor Table's Passive column, the GM clues you in on the highest rumor you beat. You can also actively hunt rumors with STAT + a relevant Skill (Library Search, Conversation, Interrogation, etc.) + 1d10 vs. the Active DV. Rumor tiers (Passive DV / Active DV): Vague 7/13, Typical 9/15, Substantial 11/17, Detailed 13/21.

Publishing Stories or Scoops — Each Rank sets your Access/Sources (who you can reach), Audience (how far a story spreads), Believability (a d10 chance the audience buys it), and Impact (how much real change a story causes). One piece of easily understood verifiable evidence raises the believe chance by 1; more than 4 distinct hard pieces raises it by 2 (these stack). LUCK can never be spent on a Believability Check. You can't publish another story on the exact same topic without new information.

Ranks 1–2: local honchos/gang lords; neighborhood audience; 2-in-10 believe; small incremental change.
Ranks 3–4: city gang honchos, minor politicians, Corp Execs; known local contributor; 3-in-10; local bad guys arrested or ousted.
Ranks 5–6: major City players and politicos, local celebrities; Citywide reach; 4-in-10; change across the City, local laws may pass.
Ranks 7–8: local Corp presidents, mayors, City celebrities; Statewide reach; 5-in-10; mid-level corporations or governments may fall, multi-city laws.
Rank 9: divisional Corp heads, State politicos; national reach; 6-in-10; national change, large corporations or governments may be toppled.
Rank 10: world leaders, major Corporation heads, world-famous celebrities; worldwide reach; 7-in-10; global change — Megacorps and governments may fall, international laws established.

exec.name: Exec
exec.tagline: Corporate power brokers and business raiders fighting to restore the rule of the Megacorps.
exec.flavorText: In the old days before the Time of the Red, you would have been a hard-driven, fast-track MBA on their way up the Corporate ladder. Sure, it was selling your soul to the Company, but face it: the Corporations ruled the world. They controlled governments, markets, nations, armies—you name it. And you knew that whoever controlled the Corporations controlled everything else. But things changed when the largest Megacorps on the planet got into a major war that was equal to anything any real national governments could have thrown down. Okay, so right now your life as a junior executive is anything but easy. There are those underneath you who'd kill for a shot at your job. Literally. There are those over you who'd kill to keep you out of their jobs. Literally. And they're not kidding about the killing—every up-and-comer in the Corporation has their own Team of Solos and Netrunners to cover important pet projects. Last week, you led a mixed team of Solos, Netrunners, and Techs on a headhunting run to "extract" a researcher from a rival company. You told yourself you joined the Corporation to make it a better place—work from the inside, you said. Or just until you could start your own Corporation that would be...a little more honest. But now you're not so sure. Your ideals are a little tarnished and things are getting pretty bleak. But you can't worry about ethics now. You've got a report due in an hour, and it looks like that guy in sales is planning to ice your database for good. You're gonna ice him first.

roleAbility.name: Teamwork
roleAbility.summary: The Exec's Role Ability is Teamwork. Just like a real corporate executive, the Exec builds a team whose members help them accomplish their goals, whether legal or not, morale permitting. Team members have a visible job description (like secretary or driver) but also have a covert roles (such as Netrunner, bodyguard, or assassin). Plus they get free housing and nice set of clothes!.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Exec Role Ability is Teamwork — the Exec builds a team whose members help accomplish their goals, morale permitting.

Signing Bonus (Rank 1): a Businesswear Jacket, Top, Bottom, and Footwear marking them as business elite (can't be resold without raising suspicion).

Corporate Housing (Rank 2): access to a Company Corporate Conapt, rent-free while they remain with the Corporation (Lifestyle is still bought separately). Rank 7 improves it to a Beaverville House in the Executive Zone; Rank 10 to a Beaverville McMansion (Executive Zone) or a Luxury Penthouse (Corporate Zone). A new Corporation matches the offer and pays to move their things.

Corporate Health Insurance: Rank 6 grants Trauma Team Silver coverage (Corp-paid monthly); Rank 8 upgrades it to Trauma Team Executive.

Team Members: Rank 3 grants 1 Team Member; Ranks 5 and 9 add one more each (max 3 at Rank 9). Team Members are built like PCs but don't improve Skills, are controlled by the GM, and can only wear Light Armorjack. The Exec picks each Team Member's class (Bodyguard, Covert Operative, Driver, Netrunner, Technician, etc.); a 1d6 roll sets their STATs and starting Loyalty is 1d6+1.

Loyalty: Team Members act based on Loyalty (caps at 10 between sessions; no cap within a session). When given a task, the GM rolls 1d6 under current Loyalty — a failed Save means they may refuse, botch, or turn on the Exec; at 0 or lower they actively betray the Exec, and ending a session below 0 means they leave. Loyalty is built by things like complimenting work (+1), perks worth 200eb+ (+4), backing them against management (+4), a 20% job cut (+6), paid time off (+6), or risking harm for them (+8); it is lost by neglect (-1), berating them (-2), forgetting their contribution or birthday (-4), broken promises (-6), throwing them under the bus (-6), or abandoning them under fire (-8).

Losing a Team Member: HR repossesses their gear and sends a replacement next session with new STATs, starting Loyalty 1, and a 200eb hiring fee to the Exec.

lawman.name: Lawman
lawman.tagline: Maximum law enforcers patrolling the mean streets and barbarian warrior highways beyond.
lawman.flavorText: In the old days before the War, they only used to shoot at cops. Now you're lucky if you just take a slug. The Street is mean these days, filled with new drugs, new gangs, and new weapons that make a Minami-10 look like a kid's toy. But even so, you're out there doing what you can to Protect—and Serve. There used to be a big City Force, but most of the Old Guard in NCPD have been thrown out on their own to keep what peace they can. The ones who remain still take the Badge seriously; they work to keep people safe and make some kind of stand against chaos. Even if you'd rather just walk a beat, if you're a professional Lawman of any stripe, you're stuck carrying at least four high-caliber weapons, most of them full-auto types, wearing a Kevlar® vest that'll stop 850ft/lbs. per square inch—and often you're still outgunned and outflanked. Half the gangs were cybered up to begin with: super speed, super reflexes, could see in the dark, carried weapons in their arms...and that was before the War and the Fall of the Towers pumped a metric ton of milspec cybertech into the Night Markets. The other half of the guys on The Street are freelance Corporate mercs who used to have jobs during the War; hired to enforce Corp armies disbanded by the New United States' goon squads. Now they're the goon squads and you're trying to keep them under control too. Used to be the Corporate Cops had heavy weapons, full combat armor, Trauma Team backup, AV-4 assault vehicles, and gyrocopters with miniguns. But the nice, clean sectors full of new office buildings and fancy restaurants—where no jacked-up psychopunk is going to ever go on a killing spree with an FN-RAL37—are mostly gone. Now you've got mostly burned-out buildings and abandoned cars, where every night is a new firefight and another great opportunity for a messy death. Or you might draw a Psycho Squad berth and get the job of hunting down heavily armed and armored cyborgs who've flipped out. A cyberpsycho can walk through machine gun fire and not even feel it, so a lot of the Psycho Squad become a bit crazy themselves; they load up with boosted reflexes, get some monstrously huge guns, and go hunt the cyborgs solo. But you're not that crazy. Yet.

roleAbility.name: Backup
roleAbility.summary: The Lawman's Role Ability is Backup. With this ability, Lawmen can call upon the help of a group of fellow officers, based on the Lawman's Rank and the conditions under which they make the call. This Backup is armed and armored based on their Rank.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Lawman's Role Ability is Backup — they can call on a group of fellow law enforcers based on their Backup Rank and the situation. Backup is armed, armored, and played by the GM. As a Lawman rises in Rank they're promoted or recruited into agencies they can call Backup from.

When in danger, as an Action you call for Backup of your Rank or lower, rolling equal to or under your Backup Rank on a d10 to get a response (abuse it and your Boss will fine you or throw you off the force). On a response, roll 1d6 for how many Rounds until they arrive; on a 6 the arriving Backup is one tier higher (at Rank 10, two groups arrive). If nobody responds, you can try again next Turn.

Each tier lists Combat Number (a combined STAT+Skill base you add 1d10 to for attack or defense — Backup can't dodge bullets), SP (Body and Head), HP, and MOVE & BODY:
Ranks 1–2: Corporate Security — 4 renta-cops on foot with Heavy Pistols and Kevlar®. Combat 8 / SP 7 / HP 20 / MOVE & BODY 4.
Ranks 3–4: Local Beat Cops — 4 cops in two Compact Groundcars, Heavy Pistols, Kevlar®. Combat 10 / SP 7 / HP 25 / 5.
Ranks 5–7: Sheriff's Department — 2 County Mounties in a High Performance Groundcar with Heavy Pistols and Assault Rifles, Heavy Armorjack. Combat 14 / SP 13 / HP 35 / 4.
Rank 8: Recovery Zone Marshal — 1 lone marshal on a Superbike with a Very Heavy Pistol, Assault Rifle, Grenade Launcher, and Flak Armor. Combat 16 / SP 15 / HP 50 / 6.
Rank 9: C-SWAT — 2 Psycho Squad hitters with Assault Rifles and Rocket Launchers in Metalgear®, arriving by AV-4. Combat 15 / SP 18 / HP 35 / 4.
Rank 10: National Law Enforcement / Interpol / FBI / Netwatch — 2 serious hitters by AV-4 with Very Heavy Pistols and Assault Rifles in Light Armorjack. Combat 14 / SP 11 / HP 35 / 6. They stay after the fight to investigate, and the same pair keeps responding to related calls until the case closes.

fixer.name: Fixer
fixer.tagline: Dealmakers, organizers, and information brokers in the post-War Midnight Markets of The Street.
fixer.flavorText: You realized fast that you weren't ever going to get a Corporate job or be tough enough to be a Solo. But you always knew you had a knack for figuring out what other people wanted, and how to get it for them. For a price, of course. Now your deals have moved past the nickel-and-dime stuff into the big time. Maybe you move illegal weapons over the border. Or steal and resell medical supplies. Perhaps you're a skill broker acting as an agent for high-priced Solos and 'Runners, or even hiring a whole Nomad pack to back a client's contracts. You buy and sell favors like an old-style Mafia godfather. You have connections into all kinds of businesses, deals, and political groups. You use your contacts and allies as part of a vast web of intrigue and coercion. If there's a hot nightclub in the City, you've bought into it. If there are military-class weapons on The Street, you smuggled ‘em in. If there's a faction war going down, you're negotiating between sides with an eye on the main chance. But you're not entirely in it for the bucks. If someone needs to get the heat off, you'll hide them. You get people housing when there isn't any, and you bring in food when the streets are blockaded. Maybe you do it because you know they'll owe you later, but you're not sure. You're one part Robin Hood and two parts AI Capone. In the past, they would have called you a crime lord. But this is the fragmented, nasty, deadly Time of the Red. So now they call you a Fixer.

roleAbility.name: Operator
roleAbility.summary: The Fixer's Role Ability is Operator. Fixers know how to get things on the black market and are adept at navigating the complex social customs of The Street, where hundreds of cultures and economic levels collide. Fixers maintain vast webs of contacts and clients who they can reach out to source goods, favors, or information. Fixers can also source desirable resources and make favorable deals.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Fixer's Role Ability is Operator. Fixers know how to get things on the black market and navigate The Street's tangle of cultures and economic levels, maintaining vast webs of contacts and clients.

Contacts & Clients — who the Fixer can reach to source goods, favors, or information (still paid for).
Reach — the highest price category the Fixer can always source; at higher Ranks they can gather other Fixers to run a Night Market, briefly making all price categories available.
Haggle — striking a deal. Roll COOL + Trading + your Operator Rank + 1d10 against the other party's COOL + Trading (+ their Operator Rank if a Fixer) + 1d10. On a success you make one deal of your Operator Rank or lower; only one Fixer deal per transaction.
Grease — blending into the many cultures on and off The Street: knowing their language, social codes, and status marks.

Ranks 1–2: local honchos/gang lords. Reach: always source Cheap and Everyday items. Haggle: ±10% of market price. Grease: your immediate neighborhood and its gangs.
Ranks 3–4: city gang honchos, minor politicians, Corp Execs. Reach: up to Expensive items. Haggle: buy 5+ of an item, get one free. Grease: one more culture plus a related language at Skill 4.
Ranks 5–6: major City players and politicos, neighborhood celebrities. Reach: once a month, organize a Night Market to source up to Super Luxury. Haggle: negotiate job pay up 20%. Grease: 3 cultures total, each with a related language at Skill 4.
Ranks 7–8: local Corp presidents, mayors, local celebrities. Reach: up to Very Expensive items. Haggle: on a Luxury/Super Luxury item, pay half now and half in a month (miss it and nobody deals again). Grease: 6 cultures total, each with a related language at Skill 4.
Rank 9: divisional Corp heads, State/City-zone politicos. Reach: up to Luxury items; can add a Midnight Market inside a Night Market. Haggle: ±20% of market price. Grease: blend with Corporate and governmental agencies.
Rank 10: world leaders, major Corporation heads, world-famous celebrities. Reach: always source up to Super Luxury. Haggle: double the pay per person on a Dangerous Job. Grease: blend seamlessly with almost any group, even secret societies or exclusive memberships.

nomad.name: Nomad
nomad.tagline: Transport experts, ultimate road warriors, pirates, and smugglers who keep the world connected.
nomad.flavorText: Years ago, the Corps drove your family off the farm. They rolled in, took over the land, and put rent-a-cops all over the place. But that was before the War. You were loners, homeless, until you created a Nomad Pack of nearly two-hundred members. Back then, your Pack was crammed into a huge, ragtag fleet of cars, vans, buses, and RVs roaming the freeways looking for supplies, odd jobs, and spare parts in a fragmented world. The Pack was your home—it had teachers, Medtechs, leaders, and mechanics—a virtual town on wheels in which everyone was related by marriage or kinship. But in the Time of the Red, your Nomad Pack has evolved. Your knowledge of roadcraft—of how to get between the safezones over the savage highways has allowed you to become the masters of getting people, supplies, and materials to a world that desperately needs them. Your cousins on the open seas have taken over the huge container ships and turned them into the Nomad convoys keeping civilization running. Your Deltajock famboys keep the supply lines to the Orbital Highriders open. If it has to get somewhere and get there safely, Nomads get the job done. Your vehicles are well-armored and bristling with stolen weapons: miniguns, rocket launchers, and the like. Every kid knows how to use a rifle, and everyone packs a knife. Like modern-day cowboys, you ride the hard trail. You've got a gun, a bike, and your Family, and that's all you need. You're a Nomad.

roleAbility.name: Moto
roleAbility.summary: The Nomad's Role Ability is Moto. Whenever a Nomad increases their Rank in Moto, they have the option of adding another stock vehicle (with minimum specs) of their Moto Rank or lower to the pool of Family vehicles they have permission to use from the Family Motorpool or to make an upgrade to one of their current vehicles. Thanks to being around vehicles since birth, Nomads are also able to drive any type of vehicle with tremendous skill.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Nomad Role Ability is Moto.

Nomad Vehicle Familiarity — A Nomad adds their Moto Rank to any Drive Land Vehicle, Pilot Air Vehicle, Pilot Sea Vehicle, Air Vehicle Tech, Land Vehicle Tech, or Sea Vehicle Tech Skill Check.

Family Motorpool — Whenever a Nomad's Role Ability Rank rises, they either add a stock vehicle (minimum specs) of their Moto Rank or lower to the vehicles they may use from the Family Motorpool, or upgrade one already-permitted Family Vehicle with a single upgrade of their Moto Rank or lower. A Nomad can have one Family Vehicle out at a time and can call the Family to swap it for another the next morning (if Family is close by). A destroyed Family Vehicle is fully repaired in a week for 500eb; daily repairs like bullet removal are the Nomad's own responsibility. At Rank 10 the Nomad is promoted to Family leadership and may have all their Family Vehicles out at once; further vehicles are bought at market price and upgrades at 1,000eb each.

Family Motorpool by Rank: 1–4 — Compact Groundcar, Gyrocopter, Jetski, Roadbike; 5–6 — Helicopter, High Performance Groundcar, Speedboat; 7–8 — AV-4, Cabin Cruiser, Superbike; 9–10 — Aerozep, AV-9, Super Groundcar, Yacht.
